name: Name expressiveness (information density)
articulated_construct: Beyond casing and blacklist checks, identifier names should carry phrase-level information through their morphemes and vocabulary, should be specific enough for the scope in which they operate, and should avoid terse or filler surfaces such as x, tmp, or data when those surfaces erase distinctions needed by readers.

axes.articulability: A prompt-based implementation can interpret whether a name fits the surrounding program concept.
axes.verifiability: A code-based implementation can measure identifier surfaces, lexical scopes, declarations, uses, collisions, and shadowing.
axes.isomorphism: Both implementations must operate on the same ctext diff and the same articulated construct; agreement is assessed separately from either channel's capability.

representation.visible_code: added lines recoverable from the diff
representation.representation_policy: Every future prompt, code, TRAIN, and heldout path must apply the exact same frozen sanitizer before consuming ctext.
representation.comparison_policy: Rows changed by sanitization are ineligible for correlation against a historical reference produced from raw ctext. A fresh prompt comparator over the same sanitized_ctext remains eligible.
not_available: unchanged declarations and uses outside diff context

executable_evidence: declaration kind and visibility surface when syntax exposes it
resolved use count and lexical reach within the added fragment
projected_relations.interpretive_boundary: The appropriate amount of specificity and any eventual scope weights are not frozen in this preparation.

executable_evidence: snake-case, camel-case, acronym, and digit morpheme segmentation
projected_relations.interpretive_boundary: Lexical diversity is evidence about surface information, not proof that the information is relevant or correct.

executable_evidence: exact conventional placeholder surfaces such as x, tmp, data, value, item, and obj
scope span and resolved-use evidence for the same declaration
projected_relations.interpretive_boundary: Short conventional names can be appropriate in tiny mathematical, iterator, callback, or receiver scopes; contextual appropriateness remains unresolved.

executable_evidence: declarations with no resolved uses in visible added code
projected_relations.interpretive_boundary: Fragment-local unresolved or unused status may be caused by unchanged code outside the diff.

executable_evidence: multiple declaration events for the same name in one qualified scope
a nested declaration sharing a name with an ancestor declaration
projected_relations.interpretive_boundary: The relations are mechanically detectable, but whether a collision or shadow is harmful is language- and context-dependent.
Determining whether a name denotes the right domain concept, communicates intent, or is misleading requires semantic interpretation not supplied by the structural capability.

synthetic_contrast_probes.positive: module-level retry_count used by several branches
synthetic_contrast_probes.negative: module-level x used by the same branches

synthetic_contrast_probes.positive: x as a one-expression mathematical lambda parameter
synthetic_contrast_probes.negative: x as a long-lived service configuration object
synthetic_contrast_probes.expected_boundary: Code can expose scope; semantic appropriateness remains hybrid.

synthetic_contrast_probes.positive: declaration and all visible uses renamed together
synthetic_contrast_probes.negative: declaration renamed while a visible lexical use retains the old surface

synthetic_contrast_probes.positive: two classes each declare a method-local status name under distinct qualified scopes
synthetic_contrast_probes.negative: two declarations of status in the same qualified scope

claim_boundary: This contract projects articulated sub-relations into executable evidence. It does not freeze an a407 candidate, establish isomorphism, or treat failed reconstruction as evidence of tacitness.
